data: Jupiter-family comet with a striking double-lobe 'rubber duck' shape. ESA's Rosetta mission orbited 67P from 2014 to 2016, accompanying it through perihelion. The Philae lander touched down in November 2014 — the first soft landing on a comet, although it bounced into shadow before its primary battery depleted.
Rosetta — ESA, 2014–16 (first orbital escort of a comet)
Philae — ESA, 12 November 2014 (first soft-landing on a comet nucleus)
67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko has e = 0.64 — a Jupiter-family comet whose orbit was reshaped by a 1959 Jupiter close approach.
Rosetta needed three Earth gravity assists and a Mars flyby to reach 67P — a 10-year cruise to catch a comet moving on its own elliptical trajectory.
How stretched the orbit is — zero is a perfect circle, one is a parabolic escape.
Steal a planet's orbital momentum on a flyby — the closest thing in space to a free lunch.
